LESSON: HISTORICAL INFORMATION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments in Africa (30 Lessons)
Topic 4.1: Historical information
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Historical information, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in Africa (30 Lessons) in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How does the past shape the present and future? 2. How significant are sources of historical information in understanding past human accounts?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign the terms related to natural and historic built environments,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Historical information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify various sources of historical information in the society,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Historical information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. distinguish between primary and secondary sources of historical information, • explore how various sources of historical information have been preserved over the years,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Historical information in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the significance of various sources of historical information in providing evidence of past human accounts. Learners are guided to: ●

   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. sign the terms related to natural and historic built environments,

   Historical information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. identify various sources of historical information in the society,

   Historical information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. distinguish between primary and secondary sources of historical information, • explore how various sources of historical information have been preserved over the years,

   Historical information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the significance of various sources of historical information in providing evidence of past human accounts. Learners are guided to: ●

   Historical information helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Historical information together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: learners develop speaking and signing skills by expressing themselves with clarity as they debate on

the significance of historical information.

● Digital Literacy: learners develop digital technology to effectively accomplish their own tasks as they find out the sources of historical

information using appropriate media.

Values:
● Patriotism: learners develop dedication as they explore how the sources of historical information have been preserved.

● Responsibility: learners diligently use appropriate print media or digital resources to find out sources of historical information.

Link to other subjects:

● English and Kenyan Sign Language: learners apply language skills as they discuss the sources of historical information in the society and

debate on the significance of historical sources of information in the society.

● Creative Arts: as learners design posters on primary and secondary sources of historical information in the society.

Suggested Learning Resources:

local and extended environment, photographs, pictures and paintings , internet sources, digital resources, approved textbooks and other printed

resources, artefacts, museum, monuments, cultural and historical sites, newspaper cuttings, libraries, posters, charts,
